about.title: California City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: California City sees its share of hard collisions each year — recent public records show 14 injury crashes, 28 people hurt, and 5 lives lost in a single year. Many of these happen on the town's busiest stretches: California City Boulevard, Route 58, Neuralia Road, and Randsburg Mojave Road, with Sunday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in the data. Whether you were driving, riding, or walking near one of these corridors, the aftermath can be overwhelming — medical visits, missed work, an insurance adjuster calling before you've even caught your breath. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney working in California, so you can get informed answers about your situation without wading through it alone. Their fee only comes from a recovery, not upfront. Reaching out early can help make sure evidence from the scene doesn't disappear before it's reviewed.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government-owned road or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can recover. What you say to an insurer in a recorded statement can be used to shift more fault onto you, which is why it's worth getting guidance before you speak with them.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning you don't pay out of pocket to have your case reviewed or represented. There's also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering under California law, so it's worth having a full conversation about what your claim may involve.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in California City?
items.answer: In most car accident cases in California, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your accident involved a government entity — for example, a poorly maintained stretch of a city or county road — that deadline can be as short as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim or shift fault onto you. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Route 58 and California City Boulevard come up a lot in local crash data — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: Corridors with higher collision counts, like Route 58 or California City Boulevard, often mean more available records, witnesses, or camera footage nearby, which can help build your case. It doesn't change the legal standards that apply, but preserving evidence from these areas quickly can matter.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in California. If you decide to move forward, attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a recovery.
